content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers

Lemon Squeezy, Stripe, PayPal, and Paddle are not just payment processors; they offer a range of services that seem appealing at first glance. However, when you dig deeper, you realize that they come with significant restrictions, limitations, and costs. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure provides a base-layer solution that empowers digital sellers to own their infrastructure, automate payment processing, and deliver products without relying on third-party platforms. This means you can deploy your own online store, set up automatic crypto payment verification, and manage your products and customers without any platform interference.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

When it comes to restricted countries, these payment processors have strict policies that leave digital sellers high and dry. For instance, Stripe operates in only 46 countries out of 195 on earth, leaving a significant portion of the global market uncovered. Similarly, PayPal has a history of suspending accounts and holding funds for up to 180 days without any appeal. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure has been designed to address the infrastructure needs of digital sellers in restricted countries, providing a permanent structural alternative that is not subject to platform policies or restrictions.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Payment speed, fees, and real costs are critical factors to consider when evaluating payment processors. While Lemon Squeezy, Stripe, and PayPal may offer fast payment processing and competitive fees, they come with significant real costs, including platform commission fees, payment processing fees, and currency conversion fees. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure provides fast and secure payment processing, with a flat 0.5% fee on all transactions, making it a more cost-effective solution for digital sellers.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure is not a workaround, but a permanent structural alternative to payment processors like Lemon Squeezy, Stripe, and PayPal.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Ownership, automation, and delivery are essential aspects of sovereign commerce infrastructure. By providing a base-layer solution, digital sellers can own their infrastructure, automate payment processing, and deliver products without relying on third-party platforms. This enables them to have full control over their business operations, reduce costs, and improve customer satisfaction. In contrast, payment processors like Lemon Squeezy, Stripe, and PayPal require digital sellers to rely on their platforms, which can lead to limited control, higher costs, and lower customer satisfaction.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

When choosing between sovereign commerce infrastructure and payment processors like Lemon Squeezy, Stripe, and PayPal, digital sellers must consider their specific needs and circumstances. If you're looking for a permanent structural alternative that provides ownership, automation, and delivery, sovereign commerce infrastructure is the clear choice. However, if you're willing to rely on third-party platforms and face restrictions, limitations, and costs, payment processors may seem appealing.
